A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FADMM research. Their main text, equations, experimental figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: Section 7 and Appendix H report original objective-versus-time experiments on sparse Fisher discriminant analysis, robust Sharpe ratio optimization, and robust sparse recovery.

after.justification: Section 7 and Appendix I report original experiments on the same three applications, including revised comparisons with FSA and an additional sparse-FDA penalty setting.

M1.justification: The FADMM-D/Q objectives, smoothing scheme, and Algorithm 1 update procedures are retained. Restoring the missing rho factor in Section 1.1's identification of h aligns it with the already-stated sparse-FDA objective; it does not establish an algorithm change. New Algorithm 2 describes a comparator.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three tasks and eight dataset configurations. Gisette is newly included in the dataset-description list but already appears in v1's figures. The additional sparse-FDA penalty value changes a setting, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds the Full Splitting Algorithm of Bot et al. (2023b), evaluated as FSA-I and FSA-II across all three applications. This introduces a distinct primal-dual competitor beyond the retained SPM and SPGM baselines. V1's SGM plot label corresponds to SPM, not a removed comparator.

E3.justification: Section 7 changes xi from 1 to 1/2 and the additive offset in chi from 10^-5 to 10^-14. The appendix changes beta0 from 0.01 to 0.001 for Sharpe ratio optimization and sparse recovery. V2 also adds rho = 10000 and FSA step sizes 10^-3 and 10^-4 within the retained evaluation design.

E4.justification: V2 extends the existing sparse-FDA regularization sweep from rho = 10, 100, 1000 to include 10000, adding a limited check of behavior under stronger sparsity penalties in Figure 4. The sparse-recovery parameter sweeps remain; no new component ablation or distribution-shift analysis appears.

E5.justification: Both versions describe random initialization and data generation without reporting seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bands. V2 does not introduce a statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds FSA trajectories throughout the experimental comparisons and eight dataset results for rho = 10000. Existing methods' objective-versus-time curves are also revised across the applications. Because reported parameter settings change, these are revised results rather than demonstrated same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: Section 1.1 corrects the mathematical specialization from h(Ax) = ||X||_1 to rho ||X||_1, making the decomposition consistent with Equation (2). The formal assumptions, convergence guarantees, complexity order, and appendix proof arguments otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, Section 1.2, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: FADMM with Dinkelbach and quadratic-transform variants, an O(1/epsilon^3) complexity guarantee, and validation on three applications. The additional comparisons do not redefine these main claims.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly interprets Nesterov smoothing as equivalent to Moreau-envelope smoothing and adds an exact-penalty rationale for choosing beta0 = 100 rho. Existing explanations of SPM behavior and the inapplicability of FADMM-Q to the sparse-recovery denominator are retained.

D1.justification: New Appendix H supplies FSA pseudocode, beta = 1, and its two constant step sizes. Section 7 changes the stated code location from supplemental material to the author's research webpage. Hardware and existing data-construction instructions are retained.

R1.justification: Remark 3.11 replaces the claim that Lemmas 3.9–3.10 are novel with attribution to standard convex analysis; Appendix C.1 adds supporting literature. V2 also expands discussion of the already-cited FSA and adds references concerning exact penalties, smoothing, and ADMM.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized rewrites to the abstract, related work, and explanatory remarks, corrects terminology and contact information, and adds acknowledgments and a conference header. The main section sequence remains, while the new FSA appendix shifts experimental material from Appendix H to I.

P2.justification: V2 expands plot legends and axes to accommodate FSA, adds the rho = 10000 figure and Algorithm 2, and moves the rho = 100 figure from the main text to the appendix. Existing eight-panel plot organization is retained, while several mathematical statements receive clearer display formatting.

improvement.justification: V2 improves attribution of the smoothing lemmas, clarifies exposition, and broadens comparison with FSA while documenting its settings. These are useful but bounded gains. The core theory is unchanged, and Algorithm 2 does not explain how FSA handles sparse FDA's negative g term, limiting confidence in that added comparison.
